content: The Antonine Plague, which occurred between 165 and 180 AD, is believed to have been caused by smallpox. In 541 AD, the Plague of Justinian emerged, marking one of the earliest recorded pandemics. The Black Death devastated populations during the 1300s, caused by Yersinia pestis. Between 1501 and 1587, typhus outbreaks were widespread. Influenza epidemics occurred in 1732-1733 and again in 1775-1776. The first cholera pandemic spanned from 1816 to 1826, followed by subsequent pandemics in 1829-1851, 1852-1860, 1863-1875, and 1899-1923. The Third Pandemic of bubonic plague began in 1855 and persisted into the 1950s. Influenza pandemics were recorded in 1847-1848, 1857-1859, and 1889-1892. The Spanish flu, caused by an avian influenza virus, occurred from 1918 to 1920, resulting in an estimated 20 to 40 million deaths globally, with more hospitalizations during World War I from this epidemic than from war-related injuries. The El Tor strain of cholera emerged in the 1960s. The HIV/AIDS pandemic began in the 1980s and continues to the present day. In Asia, the Asian flu, caused by an avian influenza virus, occurred in 1957-1958, followed by the Hong Kong flu in 1968-1969. In 1997, an avian flu outbreak was reported in China and Hong Kong. The SARS epidemic, caused by a coronavirus, occurred in 2002-2003. In Central and South America, influenza struck Hispaniola in 1493. Smallpox outbreaks occurred in Hispaniola in 1518, Mexico in 1520, and Peru between 1527 and 1530. Measles affected Mexico and Peru in 1530-1531, while typhus was reported in 1546. Influenza outbreaks occurred in Mexico and Peru in 1558-1559. Malaria became prevalent in the early 1600s, and yellow fever was reported in 1648. In Europe, the Black Death ravaged populations between 1347 and 1351. In Egypt, plague outbreaks occurred in 1801 and 1834-1836. Cholera epidemics were reported in 1831, 1848, 1865, 1881, 1902, and 1947. Falciparum malaria was prevalent between 1942 and 1944, while relapsing fever was reported in 1946. In North America, measles outbreaks were recorded in Boston, Massachusetts, in 1657, 1687, 1713, 1729, and 1739-1740. Yellow fever struck New York in 1690 and Philadelphia in 1793, 1794, 1796-1797, and 1798. Smallpox outbreaks occurred in Boston in 1721-1722 and South Carolina in 1738. Influenza epidemics were reported in 1761 and 1793. Cholera spread across the United States in 1831-1832, 1832, 1833, 1834, and 1848-1849. Typhus was reported in Philadelphia in 1837, and yellow fever affected New Orleans in 1847 and 1852. Smallpox epidemics occurred in Pennsylvania in 1860-1861 and in major cities like Philadelphia, New York City, Boston, and New Orleans between 1865 and 1873. Recurring epidemics of typhus, typhoid, scarlet fever, and yellow fever were reported during the same period. Influenza spread across North America and Europe between 1873 and 1875. The Spanish flu pandemic began in Fort Riley, Kansas, in 1918 and lasted until 1920.
